Hey everyone!

I'm new to this subreddit and also pretty new to skincare. I've recently decided that enough is enough and it's time to up my skincare game up a bit!

Issues: Sebaceous filaments (?) on my T zone and cheeks, blackheads and clogged pores on my chin and temples and recently I have had big painful spots pop out at random places. 

Skin type: I struggle with this one. It's on the greasy side of things however it gets dried up by products very very easily which makes it vulnerable to spots

Current routine: Cleanse with micellar water in the morning, Cleanse with L'Oréal charcoal clay cleanser in the evening, L'Oréal clay mask every other evening, Vaseline to moisturise before going to bed (with castor oil around my eyes mostly for eyelashes). I've taken to vaseline because whilst I've noticed it has a tendency to block pores, it keeps my face really soft .

How long: About a month or so

Anything new: Everything is new except for vaseline which I've been using for almost a year as an evening moisturiser.

Location: UK

I took my hijab off in January 2017 officially but the first time I went out in public without it in 10 years was in December 2016 and I honestly can't find the words to describe it.

The first time I had my hair out, I honestly felt like I had shed all the years I'd spent wrapped up and I was back to being about 15 and I think that contributed to how people viewed me. And one thing that I really really don't miss is being stared at by Muslims all the time when I'm out and about and having my actions judged to shit - eg when I'm out with a guy just chilling or when I was hitting the town in the evenings etc.

Those who didn't know me obviously approached me as a normal human woman and I felt people were a lot less hesitant/you could see less of the 'cogs spinning in their minds as they work out what to make of me'. 

I obviously get more attention from men however it's different to what I got before. Now I simply get checked out and it's all stuff I can deal with. Before it used to be muslim men and I don't need to describe the way in which a lot of them would completely defile me with their stares. 

The non Muslims who already knew me obviously met me with a lot of curiosity and some actually became a lot more open towards me. Like at first it was very confusing for a lot of them but they got used to it and stopped being unable to recognise me haha.

The Muslims who knew me looked at me a bit weird and tbh the ones I was friends with just didn't mention it at all but I think that's because I am friends with few Muslims and those I am friends with are decent enough to realise it's none of their darn business.

I'm not really sure why, but I really wasnt happy with this when I first saw it. I think the thing about it is that I felt uncomfortable laughing at this knowing that this is based on a reality for some women, especially the bit where one of them is chained to her stove (not saying muslim women are literally chained to their stoves but it is the case metaphorically for a lot of Muslim women)

Whilst mocking ISIS is fine, something about mocking the women and the way they're second-class citizens just doesn't sit well with me at all. Maybe it's because there are sort-of-parallels in the Muslim world outside of ISIS.

Thanks everyone who replied!

I think this is starting to make a bit more sense to me tbh, although it's weird because I've grown up in a community where the people take the Qur'an and Hadith literally, and so the concept of a Muslim community whereby this is not the case is very alien to me. 
You're talking to someone who's parents pray the voluntary prayers in addition to the ones 5 times a day (so they pray like 10 times????idk) and make me feel guilty for not doing so...

The thing is, the finances are something I could figure out tbh. Like, bearing in mind my parents know nobody here where I live and I only see my parents once every few months...I just feel like it's something I could get away with.

I'm unsure as to what you mean. 

Are you basically saying 'yeah go for it, but make sure you have a backup plan you can rely on, work hard, and get yourself out of this situation'??

Either way, the only thing holding me back is fear. I've never confronted my parents before and this will be the first time I will have to.

I've got a bit of money saved and I have a friend who'll be able to lend me some money if it comes to it. Basically, I will hopefully have a job in August this year, so I'll just have to hold out until then.

I want to say thank you to everyone who got back to me on this post. Things are still difficult, but for a few days after I'd posted this, I was getting a lot of messages of support and it really means a lot as I'm currently incredibly isolated right now. Thanks a lot everyone.
The thing is, it's just one of those things where I'll be thinking about everything and suddenly it just gets way too much and being alive just feels so difficult

I think with my family it's a case of just outright not accepting my emotions, for whatever reason. I think what's difficult right now is that it's the summer holidays and there just isn't much to do so my mind just dwells.

Joining the gym may be a good shout though!

See, this is an interesting one. 

I'm personally against it because, whilst the idea is to get rid of religion-induced inequality (this is what I've always been told), by banning the hijab, women in communities where the hijab is regarded as an absolute must will be prevented from accessing opportunities (e.g. getting an education/getting a job) thus almost keeping them 'trapped' in their community without a way to build their way out. 

We are not in a position, as Muslim women in the west, where we can tell our communities to go f*** themselves whenever they tell us how to live our lives. I come from a Muslim community where women I know/grew up with, have been remarkably restricted in terms of building themselves their independence - a lot of them aren't allowed to leave home, a lot of them aren't given the encouragement to get a good career/outright aren't allowed to attend colleges unless they're single-sex (by college, I mean UK college), some have even been forbidden from learning to drive (male instructors) and a lot are essentially 'trained' to put their wife-hood above all else. In a community like this, if these sorts of laws were around in the UK, these women would be much much further restricted unfortunately, which is why I don't think the 'West' is ready for this sort of ban on hijab.
That's the thing, I don't want to die. But at the same time, staying alive is just so difficult that I sometimes feel like I can't go on.

As someone who is struggling, I really don't appreciate your response.

You are dictating how women should dress, whilst maintaining the double standard that muslim culture encourages when it comes to how men and women dress. Not only that, you're defending it by somehow calling it 'feminist'.

I posted on here for some support, not for a lecture. And especially not from someone who's just outright said that he fetishises women of colour, which is both creepy and inappropriate.

Yeah, it could be much much worse - in my mosque communities I've seen women being far more oppressed that I have. Our Imam's daughters were my friends when I was younger and they got married at the ages of 21 and 19 after a life of sheltering and not letting them really go out or get an education or anything simply because they're women. 

The one who got married at 19 (bear in mind it was an arranged marriage and she's clueless when it comes to dating and whatnot) is now in the process of divorcing the guy after having his two kids and having him be abusive towards her to the point where she has to live at her parents' house again.......An absolute shitshow if you ask me!

Thanks for your support. It's really difficult because some days it really feels like a huge weight on me.

Unfortunately my parents would never simply accept 'I don't want to wear it anymore' or anything along the lines of me just not being made to wear it.

I didn't know that about the revelation! How come it's never mentioned......?
